\section[\texorpdfstring{\ru{выпускник} (vypuskník)}{выпускник (vypuskník)}]{\ru{выпускник} (vypuskník) — a school-leaver, a graduate}

\label{lesson:RU-C308-vypusknik}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Russian for to quit, then the Russian for an inheritance.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ru{выпускник}}
\textbf{\ru{выпускник}} (\emph{vypuskník}) — \textquotedblleft{}a school-leaver, a graduate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ru{Выпускники} \ru{подарили} \ru{учителю} \ru{цветы}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Vypusknikí podaríli uchítelyu tsvetý.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The school-leavers gave the teacher flowers.
\end{quote}

A woman is \emph{\ru{выпускница}}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{\ru{выпускник}} is built on \emph{\ru{выпуск}} \textquotedblleft{}a graduating class\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{\ru{выпускать}} \textquotedblleft{}to let out\textquotedblright{}, whose root is Proto-Slavic \emph{pustiti} \textquotedblleft{}to let go\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ru{поступать} (postupát)}{поступать (postupát)}]{\ru{поступать} (postupát) — to enter, to get into (a university); to act}

\label{lesson:RU-C308-postupat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Russian for an inheritance, then the Russian for a school-leaver.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ru{поступать}}
\textbf{\ru{поступать}} (\emph{postupát}) — \textquotedblleft{}to enter, to get into (a university); to act\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ru{Брат} \ru{поступил} \ru{в} \ru{университет}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Brat postupíl v universitét.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My brother got into university.
\end{quote}

Imperfective; perfective \emph{\ru{поступить}} (\emph{postupít}). \emph{\ru{Поступить} \ru{в}} + accusative. Also \textquotedblleft{}to act\textquotedblright{}: \emph{\ru{он} \ru{поступил} \ru{честно}}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{\ru{поступать}} is built on \emph{\ru{по}-} and \emph{\ru{ступать}} \textquotedblleft{}to step\textquotedblright{}, the root of \emph{\ru{ступень}} \textquotedblleft{}a step\textquotedblright{}, Proto-Slavic \emph{stǫpenĭ} (EtymDB): to step in.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ru{оканчивать} (okánchivat)}{оканчивать (okánchivat)}]{\ru{оканчивать} (okánchivat) — to finish, to graduate from}

\label{lesson:RU-C308-okanchivat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Russian for a school-leaver, then the Russian for to enter.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ru{оканчивать}}
\textbf{\ru{оканчивать}} (\emph{okánchivat}) — \textquotedblleft{}to finish, to graduate from\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ru{Он} \ru{окончил} \ru{школу} \ru{в} \ru{прошлом} \ru{году}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{On okónchil shkólu v próshlom godú.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He finished school last year.
\end{quote}

Imperfective; perfective \emph{\ru{окончить}} (\emph{okónchit}). It takes the accusative: \emph{\ru{окончить} \ru{университет}}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{\ru{оканчивать}} is built on \emph{\ru{о}-} and \emph{\ru{конец}} \textquotedblleft{}end\textquotedblright{}, inherited through Old East Slavic \emph{konĭcĭ} from Proto-Slavic \emph{konĭcĭ} \textquotedblleft{}end\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ru{диплом} (diplóm)}{диплом (diplóm)}]{\ru{диплом} (diplóm) — a degree, a diploma}

\label{lesson:RU-C308-diplom}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Russian for to enter, then the Russian for to finish.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ru{диплом}}
\textbf{\ru{диплом}} (\emph{diplóm}) — \textquotedblleft{}a degree, a diploma\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ru{Она} \ru{получила} \ru{диплом} \ru{врача}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Oná poluchíla diplóm vrachá.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
She got her medical degree.
\end{quote}

Masculine. \emph{\ru{Дипломная} \ru{работа}} — a final-year thesis.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{\ru{диплом}} is usually traced through Latin \emph{diplōma} to Greek \emph{díplōma} \textquotedblleft{}a paper folded double\textquotedblright{}; EtymDB lists the Russian word with no parent.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ru{аттестат} (attestát)}{аттестат (attestát)}]{\ru{аттестат} (attestát) — a school-leaving certificate}

\label{lesson:RU-C308-attestat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Russian for to finish, then the Russian for a degree.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ru{аттестат}}
\textbf{\ru{аттестат}} (\emph{attestát}) — \textquotedblleft{}a school-leaving certificate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ru{В} \ru{июне} \ru{мы} \ru{получили} \ru{аттестаты}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{V iyúne my poluchíli attestáty.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In June we got our school-leaving certificates.
\end{quote}

\emph{\ru{Аттестат} \ru{зрелости}} — the full name, \textquotedblleft{}certificate of maturity\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{\ru{аттестат}} goes back to Latin \emph{attestātus} \textquotedblleft{}confirmed\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), from \emph{attestārī} \textquotedblleft{}to bear witness\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{testis} \textquotedblleft{}a witness\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
